claims.nodeLabel: Council Bluffs, Iowa molten metal fall, 17 December 1977
claims.sourceText: Sol Foundation Policy Briefing No. 3, citing the Daily Nonpareil (18 December 1977) and Greg Jerrett, 'Mystery at Big Lake: Fire in the Sky', Daily Nonpareil, 16 May 2004
claims.text: Five independent groups of witnesses observed a red luminous mass descending from approximately 500-600 feet near a park in Council Bluffs on the evening of 17 December 1977; the assistant fire chief described a roughly four-by-six-foot mass of molten metal 'running, boiling down the edges of the levee'; police photographed the scene.

claims.sourceText: The Sol Foundation Science and Policy Briefings No. 3, April 2026, summarising the Nolan/Vallee paper
claims.text: The Council Bluffs analysis found no anomalous isotopic values but incomplete mixing of the constituent metals, indicating an industrial process of unknown origin, and ruled out meteorite, satellite/spacecraft, aircraft-debris, molten-metal-dumping and thermite explanations.

claims.sourceText: Sol Foundation Policy Briefing No. 3, April 2026, citing contemporaneous newspaper records
claims.text: The Council Bluffs event of 17 December 1977 was witnessed by five independent groups, photographed by police, and described contemporaneously by the assistant fire chief as a four-by-six-foot mass of molten metal 'running, boiling down the edges of the levee'; press reporting appeared in the Daily Nonpareil on 18 December 1977 and the Des Moines Register on 26 January 1978.

claims.nodeLabel: Nolan Laboratory, Stanford University School of Medicine
claims.sourceText: Sol Foundation Policy Briefing No. 3 summarising Nolan, Vallee, Jiang & Lemke (2022)
claims.text: The laboratory applied SIMS and MIBI to the Council Bluffs samples at 200 nanometre lateral resolution and five-nanometre depth increments, finding no anomalous isotopic values but incomplete mixing of the constituent metals.

claims.nodeLabel: Nolan, Vallee, Jiang & Lemke (2022), Progress in Aerospace Sciences 128:100788
claims.sourceText: Sol Foundation Policy Briefing No. 3, April 2026, summarising the paper
claims.text: Meteorite, satellite/spacecraft debris, aircraft debris, dumped molten metal and thermite hypotheses were each examined and ruled out on physical grounds; the thermite exclusion rests on the absence of aluminium oxide in the SIMS diatomic analysis.

claims.text: The analysis found no anomalous isotopic values but incomplete mixing of the metals in the once-molten mass, indicating an industrial process of unknown origin.

claims.sourceText: Sol Foundation Science and Policy Briefings No. 3, Executive Summary
claims.text: The briefing states that the SIMS and MIBI analyses found no anomalous isotopic values but that the metals in the once-molten mass were mixed incompletely, 'indicating an industrial process of unknown, and potentially perplexing, origin'.

claims.nodeLabel: Sol Foundation Science and Policy Briefing No. 3 (April 2026)
claims.sourceText: Notes 11 and 12, Sol Foundation Briefing No. 3
claims.text: The briefing states that iron meteorites contain 5-40% nickel while the Council Bluffs sample had only trace amounts, and that aluminium oxide - the necessary byproduct of a thermite reaction - would have been observed as a diatomic in the SIMS analysis and was not.

claims.nodeLabel: Sol Foundation Science and Policy Briefing No. 3 (April 2026)
claims.text: The briefing records that no foundries in the region were operating on the day of the incident and that no airports or military facilities in the region reported aviation incidents before, during or after.
